output.title: When versioned answers stop working
output.body:
When your versioned answers start failing, the problem is usually not the wording. It is the workflow around them. FAQ entries, product docs, and customer reply templates stop holding up when customer context changes, questions drift, or the source material ages faster than you can rewrite it. That gives you a bounded decision: keep re-checking and rewriting by hand, hire someone to maintain the material, or automate part of the process.

The practical test is simple. Pick one recurring question that keeps coming back by email, support ticket, or chat. Count how often the answer needs a manual correction, and check whether the source documents are current, digital, and consistent. If the answer depends on scattered files, scanned pages, or conflicting versions, automation will not fix the source problem. It only helps if there is something stable to retrieve from. That is the unglamorous part, but it saves expensive guessing.

Where AI can fit is a grounded knowledge assistant: it looks in approved company material first, retrieves the relevant context, and shows sources so you can spot outdated or conflicting information before anything is sent. In Bareni’s self-built demo, that retrieval pattern works locally on synthetic data; it is not a customer deployment, and the public route is locked. So the useful question is not “Can AI answer this?” but “Can I give it clean enough source material to answer it safely?”

Next step: run a short diagnostic on one workflow, one question set, and one source base. If the material is tidy enough, you can decide whether a pilot is worth defining. If not, keep it manual and save the automation for a better case.
